chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Abī Khālid, from Ḥumrān, who said:
I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about giving the adhān while seated. He said: No one gives the adhān while seated except a rider or a sick person.
Thus, the proper approach regarding this report is that we carry it upon a kind of recommendation rather than obligation.

key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation or preferred status in law

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to give the adhān while sitting according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling of giving the adhān while seated, stating that it is done seated only by a rider or a sick person. The concluding statement clarifies that this is to be understood as a recommendation of preferred practice, not as a matter of obligation.
